mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 1.75% over the prior 4 months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over the past 4 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar 4-month pre-rising period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration in the nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% suggests rising labor market confidence, which precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth rate > 0.5% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 8 consecutive months of PAYEMS > 0.5% growth, SPX 20-day returns are not positive (mean < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) above 2% for two consecutive months indicates strengthening consumer demand, which typically drives positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: During the two-month high-demand window, SPX 5-day returns are negative on average (mean < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) below 105 combined with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests supply-side constraints, which can produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 105 and UNRATE is declining, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (mean >= 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% triggers a preemptive rate cut expectation, which can result in positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL drops below 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During CPIAUCSL < 2% window, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% indicate a labor market cooling, which is associated with negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 4% for two months, 60-day forward returns are not negative (mean >= 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both retail sales (HOUST) and manufacturing activity (RSAFS) above 105 suggests dual-demand expansion, which can produce positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: During periods of high HOUST and RSAFS, SPX 20-day returns are not positive (mean < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (regime_hint: 'late-cycle expansion'), the combination of a high industrial production index (INDPRO > 108) and a rising consumer confidence index (not available in evidence, so this will be omitted) would typically precede a short-term S&P 500 pullback, resulting in negative 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During the late-cycle expansion with INDPRO > 108, 5-day forward returns are not negative (mean > 0).
